tests.name: Cozen’s Test
tests.procedure: Patient makes a fist, pronates forearm, and extends wrist against examiner resistance with elbow in 90° flexion.
tests.positiveImplication: Sudden severe pain at lateral epicondyle indicates lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow).

tests.name: Mill’s Sign
tests.procedure: Patient closes hand, examiner fully extends elbow, pronates forearm, and flexes wrist.
tests.positiveImplication: Pain over lateral epicondyle during passive stretch confirms lateral epicondylitis.

tests.name: Maudsley’s Test
tests.procedure: Examiner resists extension of middle finger (third digit) distal to PIP joint.
tests.positiveImplication: Pain over lateral epicondyle indicates extensor digitorum involvement.

tests.name: Tinel’s Sign at Cubital Tunnel
tests.procedure: Examiner lightly taps ulnar nerve in groove between medial epicondyle and olecranon.
tests.positiveImplication: Electric shock or tingling sensation radiating into 4th and 5th digits indicates ulnar neuropathy.

tests.name: Elbow Flexion Test
tests.procedure: Patient holds elbow in maximal flexion with wrist in neutral for up to 3 minutes.
tests.positiveImplication: Numbness or paresthesias in ulnar nerve distribution indicates cubital tunnel syndrome.

tests.name: Valgus Stress Test
tests.procedure: Forearm supinated, elbow flexed to 25°–30°. Examiner stabilizes arm and applies valgus stress to forearm.
tests.positiveImplication: Pain or excessive medial joint opening/laxity indicates medial collateral ligament (MCL) injury.

tests.name: Moving Valgus Stress Test
tests.procedure: Examiner applies constant valgus torque while flexing and extending elbow between 30° and 120°.
tests.positiveImplication: Pain maximal between 70° and 120° indicates MCL tear.
